affiliations.organization_name_as_found: Romania's press attaché in Washington; the Legation's financial advisor
affiliations.role_title: Press attaché; financial adviser and counsellor
affiliations.date_precision: A scholarly note places George Boncescu as press attaché in Washington from 1927 to 1938, briefly in Paris in April 1938, and back in Washington as financial counsellor in September 1938; it does not state when that post ended.
affiliations.research_notes: The rare Boncescu name, Romanian subject matter, Washington setting, and independent exact-name identification of George N. Boncescu in the OSS Romanian section support the match. Because the diplomatic source omits the middle initial and does not bridge the 1938-to-OSS chronology, the affiliation remains qualified and is excluded from default analytics.

affiliations.date_precision: Recorded as civilian-occupation code 105 at Army entry on May 12, 1942; no employer, office, industry, duties, or start date is named.

affiliations.date_precision: Recorded as civilian-occupation code 007 at Army entry on July 13, 1943; the code does not distinguish among the three occupations or name an employer, specialty, workplace, or start date.
affiliations.research_notes: Exact private-identifier and exact-name agreement confirm identity. The record also carries education code 2, meaning two years of high school; no scientific employer or educational institution is inferred.

affiliations.role_title: Bachelor of Music student; Japanese-language student

affiliations.research_notes: This is a student affiliation, not employment. The exact uncommon name, contemporary Michigan record, and University of Rochester description of her OSS service provide a high-confidence identity match.

claims.claim_text: The indexed George N. Boncescu is identified with high confidence as the person independently listed in a scholarly concordance as serving in the OSS Romanian section.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The visually checked NARA index and the Wilson Center concordance share his uncommon exact full name; the concordance supplies the OSS Romanian-section role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from an uncommon exact full name plus a matching OSS organizational context.
claims.temporal_assessment: The concordance cites a 1944 VENONA reference; it does not state recruitment or separation dates.
claims.match_notes: This establishes person-level identity and OSS context. It does not by itself link him to the same-name Romanian diplomat or establish a pre-OSS affiliation.
